label: prop:collatz-no-cycles
title: Balanced-holonomy cycle exclusion: coprimality of $[2]_q$ and $[3]_q$
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q and Skein module \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. The Skein-Collatz map \mathcal{C}_q has no periodic orbit of balanced multiplicative holonomy — none with A = \prod_i a_i = 1 — other than the degenerate fixed point. As an identity in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], [3]_q^{k_{\mathrm{odd}}} = [2]_q^{k} has no solution with k_{\mathrm{odd}} \geq 1, by coprimality of [2]_q and [3]_q. This does not hold for a real value of q: at the plastic number q = \rho \approx 1.32472 (the real root of q^3 = q + 1), (1 + q + q^2)^3 = (1 + q)^5. The cycle exclusion holds for every real q > 0 all the same, because the additive part of a cycle with an odd step is positive (see the proof).

The affine (A \neq 1) case is settled in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] as well, by a different argument: the only periodic orbits of \mathcal{C}_q there are \{0\}, the odd fixed point \{-q^{-2}\} and the fundamental cycle \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\} (see the proof). What stays open in the q-Collatz conjecture is convergence, i.e. the absence of divergent orbits (contact boundary).
